1: Two lines run close together over a short distance, without touching
2: They couple twice: through the electric field (a capacitance C) and the magnetic field (M)
3: Forward wave IN → OUT: at the CPL end both currents point the same way, at the ISO end they cancel
4: Reflected wave OUT → IN: the main current turns, so does the M part. Now they add at ISO, the 50 Ω eats it.
5: So CPL sees only the forward wave, about 10 dB weaker. Turned around, the same part sees only the reflection.
